title: Glint
description: Tracing a server-side analytics prototype from request metadata through ingestion, PostgreSQL and a chart dashboard, with simulated data made explicit.
techStack: Next.js, TypeScript, Vercel Edge Middleware, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Recharts, Cloudflare Workers
status: Local dashboard candidate 7e33b73; sample charts and responsive controls verified, release pending.

blocks.heading: Explore the measurement pipeline
blocks.body: Glint explores capturing request metadata on the server, storing it behind an API and presenting it in a dashboard. Its demonstration includes simulated traffic from a scheduled Cloudflare Worker. Session duration and network-speed values in the middleware are also randomly generated. Those values are not measurements of real visitor behaviour.

items.alt: Local Glint dashboard with a visible visit-event chart and a prominent synthetic-data notice.
items.caption: Unreleased local dashboard at 7e33b73. Every displayed value is from the labelled synthetic example, not a real audience.

blocks.heading: Follow a request into a chart
blocks.caption: These links identify the unchanged collection baseline. The local 7e33b73 dashboard candidate adds the explicit data-source and request-state work below. No database or collection operation was verified.

steps.label: Request boundary
steps.detail: Middleware reads request headers and starts four API posts for average, location, referral and traffic payloads. It excludes API, Next.js and favicon paths from its matcher.

steps.label: Ingestion boundary
steps.detail: The route checks the payload type and required location/referral/traffic fields, then calls the appropriate Prisma model. Middleware does not write directly to PostgreSQL.

steps.label: Storage boundary
steps.detail: Separate models store average, location, referral, traffic, session and device records. This is not a single partitioned events table.

steps.label: Presentation boundary
steps.detail: The average-metrics component loads an API snapshot, groups records by date in the browser and passes it to Recharts. The reviewed component fetches on mount.

blocks.heading: Keep demonstration data separate from evidence
blocks.context: A regularly populated dashboard makes the charting pipeline visible, but plausible-looking numbers can suggest a real audience.

options.label: Present generated values as audience metrics
options.detail: The chart would look active while obscuring the provenance of its values.

options.label: Describe the prototype and identify synthetic inputs
options.detail: The local dashboard starts from a fixed synthetic example with persistent provenance text. Stored snapshots are a separate explicit selection and never silently fall back to sample values.

blocks.outcome: The portfolio does not use the demonstration as evidence of customer volume, engagement or a measured performance gain.

blocks.heading: Delivery is a boundary still to strengthen
blocks.body: The middleware starts its posts without awaiting them. That avoids deliberately holding the response open for ingestion, but it does not establish zero latency or guarantee that a serverless runtime will finish those requests. Delivery lifetime and failure handling need explicit verification before this becomes production analytics.

blocks.heading: Make query scope legible
blocks.body: The local dashboard separates six independently scoped requests, uses no-store, aborts on view changes and times out after ten seconds. Empty, malformed, HTTP-failure and network-error states are distinct. Seven or fourteen captured dates are selected from a snapshot, not an arbitrary reporting range. Dates aggregate in UTC, and expandable value tables expose the displayed records. Random session/network fields are omitted from this presentation. Stored-data branches have mock coverage only.

blocks.heading: What the current source proves
blocks.body: The local product pass has nineteen tests, TypeScript, source lint and a production build passing, with zero findings in its full and production dependency audits. Final mounted desktop and 390px browser checks show a visible area plot, twenty-four hourly bars and labelled axes. Seven/fourteen captured-date selection and overflow checks passed. An earlier blank capture was withdrawn; the cause was not conclusively isolated. No stored-data or database operation was exercised, and sample-mode checks do not certify the unchanged collection backend.
